logline: On Trikūṭa, Gajendra leads the herd to the lotus lake, where they enjoy the cool water—until a powerful crocodile suddenly seizes his leg.

source.edition: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Canto 8; passage checked against Vedabase verse pages (copyrighted translation not reused)
source.verification_notes: S01 uses only 8.2.1–4. Verse 1 identifies Śukadeva speaking to a king and Trikūṭa amid the Ocean of Milk; verses 2–3 describe the three gold, silver and iron peaks, other gem-rich peaks, vegetation and waterfalls; verse 4 describes ocean waves and emerald-colored foothills. These are originally written spoken paraphrases, not verbatim verse translations. Verse-level anchors point to the combined 8.2.2–3 page where appropriate. The subsequent garden, herd and lake are reserved for S02 and later scenes. S02 paraphrases the separate bird-rich valleys and clear waters (8.2.7–8), Varuṇa's garden Ṛtumat with year-round fruit and flowers (8.2.9–13), and its golden-lotus lake with other water lilies, bees, water birds, fish, tortoises and flowering banks (8.2.14–19). Waterway and shoreline blocking are editorial staging, not claimed scripture; Gajendra and the crocodile are reserved for later scenes. S03 retells SB 8.2.20 (elephant leader and thorny forest), 8.2.21 (fierce animals flee from his scent), 8.2.22 (smaller animals roam without fear), and the combined 8.2.23–24 (female elephants, calves, heavy steps, heat, bees, thirst and lotus-pollen breeze leading to the lake bank). Each line is independently phrased and verse-attributed. No water entry or attack is moved into S03. S04 paraphrases SB 8.2.25–26: Gajendra enters the clear, cool lotus-pollen lake, drinks with his trunk and bathes, then sprinkles female elephants and their young and helps them drink and bathe. Verse 26's reflection on attachment to his family/heedlessness of hardship is condensed to a gentle observation, without declaring love itself wrongful or inventing foreknowledge. The crocodile grips him in 8.2.27 and must not appear in S04. S05 is a deliberately shortened 30-second original cinematic bridge rather than a distinct event described between verses 8.2.26 and 8.2.27. Its one scriptural-paraphrase line revisits Gajendra's absorption in the herd (8.2.26); subsequent calf placement, falling droplets, surface ripples and apparent stillness are explicitly original dramatization/atmosphere, not assertions about the source. Verse 8.2.27 begins the sudden crocodile foot-grip; S05 does not depict advance, shadow, underwater approach, warning or attack. S06 begins the crocodile's first appearance and foot-grip in SB 8.2.27, including Gajendra's immediate exertion to get free. Verse 8.2.28 confirms the female elephants' cries and the other elephants' attempt to help; only the beginning of their approach is dramatized here. The detailed failed pull from behind belongs to the S01E02 opening, while the thousand-year struggle belongs to 8.2.29 and later. The specific left-foreleg choice, water splashes and shot direction are original staging, not verse facts. No violence is depicted graphically.

core_preserved: Śukadeva addresses a king while describing Trikūṭa, a large mountain surrounded by the Ocean of Milk (SB 8.2.1).
Trikūṭa has three principal peaks of gold, silver and iron, plus mineral- and jewel-rich secondary peaks, trees, vines, shrubs and waterfalls (SB 8.2.2–3).
Waves of the Ocean of Milk wash the foot of the mountain where emeralds make the ground green (SB 8.2.4).
The wooded valleys and clear, gem-edged waters below Trikūṭa are described before Ṛtumat garden (SB 8.2.7–8).
Ṛtumat belongs to Varuṇa and includes trees that fruit and flower across seasons, including mango, coconut, aśoka and campaka (SB 8.2.9–13).
The garden lake has golden lotuses, other water lilies, bees, swans, cranes, fish, tortoises and abundant flowering banks (SB 8.2.14–19).
A powerful leader walks with female elephants through thorny, overgrown forest and breaks branches (SB 8.2.20).
Lions, tigers, rhinoceroses and large snakes flee, but elsewhere deer, rabbits, monkeys and other small animals are not afraid (SB 8.2.21–22).
Female elephants and young follow the perspiring leader; bees circle near him, and the scent of lotus pollen travels from the lake as the thirsty herd reaches its bank (SB 8.2.23–24).
Gajendra bathes in the lotus-pollen-filled lake, drinks cool clear water with his trunk until satisfied, and is refreshed (SB 8.2.25).
Gajendra lifts and sprays lake water with his trunk and helps female elephants and their young drink and bathe, absorbed in his family and heedless of the effort (SB 8.2.26).
A strong crocodile unexpectedly grasps Gajendra's leg in the water; despite his great power, Gajendra must struggle to free himself (SB 8.2.27).
Female elephants cry out and the other elephants come to help; the source's unsuccessful attempted rescue is deferred to the beginning of S01E02 (SB 8.2.28).
changes: The narrator speaks an original accessible retelling rather than directly quoting Śukadeva or a modern published English translation.
The gold-left, silver-center, iron-right arrangement, aerial camera moves, ambient sound and transitions are original visual staging decisions; scripture does not assign peak positions.
The cosmic scale is conveyed pictorially without asserting a literal real-world map. No later garden, animals, lake or crocodile events are moved into S01.
S02 condenses the long scriptural plant and bird lists into a few representative species; it does not invent an incident or named animal character.

The camera path from the previously established emerald foothills into the valley garden, the approach bank and the lake's on-screen geography are original staging decisions rather than stated map directions.

All S02 dialogue is original narrator paraphrase. Varuṇa is identified as owner but not depicted giving newly invented dialogue; Gajendra, the herd and the crocodile do not appear before their later scene.
Gajendra is visually identified with the scriptural elephant leader; his narrated name is an identification, not a new incident. The full zoological lists are selectively condensed.

The elephant and herd remain non-speaking. Forest positions, specific plants broken by the walk, Gajendra's trunk gesture at the breeze, and exact approach-bank blocking are production staging decisions, not verbatim verse facts.

The 60-second scene ends with the herd at the bank because 8.2.23–24 already places them there; entering the water, drinking, bathing and the crocodile attack are deliberately reserved for later scenes.
S04 presents the bathing, drinking and sharing of water as three continuous editorial shots at the same stable lake bank; shot order and exact blocking are cinematic staging decisions.
The source's reflection on Gajendra's attachment and disregard for hardship is conveyed gently without manufacturing a warning, malicious creature, divine punishment or spoken elephant dialogue.
No crocodile, threatening water shadow, attack or unseen predator is scripted in S04: the source first places the crocodile grip in 8.2.27, reserved for S06.

S05 adds only an original, non-predatory 30-second closing-lake pause after the verse-26 water-sharing action; its mother/calf blocking, last droplets and fading surface ripples are clearly labeled original dramatization, not a new scriptural episode.

The S05 working title is metaphorical. It does not license a crocodile underwater POV, stealth approach, ominous eye or unseen shadow; the crocodile's first on-screen grip belongs only to verse 8.2.27 in S06.

The old uniform 60-second S05 editorial plan is reduced to 30 seconds to avoid duplicating verse-26 material or adding unsupported plot. The eventual episode timing/validator preferred total must be rebalanced by a separate reviewed editorial decision, not padded automatically.

For continuity, the crocodile is staged on Gajendra's left foreleg in the lake's near shallows, but the scripture identifies only his leg/foot without specifying a side. No predator is shown before the sudden grip.

The first capture is depicted in wide, non-graphic compositions; realistic splashing and sound effects are production staging, and one narrator line explicitly labels water movement as original dramatization rather than a verse quotation.

The herd's distressed reaction begins in S06, but the coordinated failed rescue of 8.2.28, advantage of water and land, and the thousand-year struggle of 8.2.29 are intentionally reserved for S01E02, rather than staged twice.

S06 remains a 60-second editorial action scene, producing a six-scene total of 330 seconds rather than the current preferred 360. A separate GM-RET-001 editorial and validation review must resolve the target mismatch without invented combat or filler. Preserve episode authoring status partial_scene_draft.
adaptation.fidelity_note: S01–S05's original canon-backed script and marked cinematic insert remain unchanged. S06 uses independently written three-language narration based on SB 8.2.27–28, distinguishing the crocodile's sudden leg-grip from original camera, designated leg, splash and sound staging. The animals never speak human dialogue, the grip is child-safe/non-graphic, and the episode stops before prolonged struggle. This is not a verbatim modern English translation.

characters.description: Offscreen voice for the scriptural geographic prologue; not a visually present human or Śukadeva impersonation.
characters.voice_direction: Calm, clear and warmly curious, naming the three peaks distinctly and allowing waterfall and shoreline sounds to breathe; no voice actor has been selected.

characters.description: The enormous naturally quadrupedal leader of the Trikūṭa elephant herd, visually introduced in S03; no crown, human actions, or spoken animal lines. Preserve approved character-bible anatomy in future visual work.
characters.voice_direction: No dialogue or voice casting in S01–S03. Natural animal calls belong in ambience/SFX; a later inner-prayer voiceover requires its own explicit source and performance approval.

characters.description: A powerful natural crocodile, visually introduced only with its sudden grip on Gajendra's leg in S06. No approved portrait, no costume, no human mouth. The separate Hūhū identity is not disclosed or personified in this scene.
characters.voice_direction: Non-speaking wild animal. Water and animal noises, if produced later, are nonverbal SFX; no voice ID, TTS line or lip-sync is assigned.

scenes.title: The three peaks of Trikūṭa
scenes.setting: An island mountain surrounded by the Ocean of Milk: distant three-peak skyline, gem-studded smaller slopes, waterfalls and emerald-colored foothills. The garden, herd and freshwater lake are not shown yet.
scenes.action: A narrated opening vista moves from the Ocean of Milk and the immense mountain, through its three defining gold/silver/iron peaks, to the forested, waterfall-filled slopes and emerald shoreline. No named character appears on screen; later scenes will establish the separate Ṛtumat garden and the lake.
nonverbal_beats: Begin with a quiet, wide expanse of the Ocean of Milk before revealing Trikūṭa rising from it.

Read the three principal peaks in one silhouette; for a stable editorial screen map, stage gold left, silver center, iron right. Their screen positions are an original staging decision, not claimed as a verse detail.
Use one sustained rushing-water sound transition from jewel-bearing smaller peaks to waterfalls.
Finish with waves meeting emerald-green foothills. Do not show the Ṛtumat garden, Gajendra, herd, crocodile or the later freshwater lake yet.

shots.action: Open on an immense milky ocean, tilt up to Trikūṭa rising from its island; use offscreen narration L001–L002. No people or animals.
shots.camera: Extreme-wide 16:9 aerial establishing shot, slow rise; preserve mountain center and ocean around it.
shots.sound: Ocean surf underneath narrator; a restrained original ambient musical bed. No voices besides NARRATOR.

shots.action: Reveal the three primary peaks together and distinguish gold, silver and iron while narrator says L003–L004. Gold/silver/iron left-to-right is continuity staging only.
shots.camera: Wide frontal composition and slow lateral drift; keep all three peaks in a single stable view.
shots.sound: Wind at altitude and delicate, non-diegetic atmosphere under the narration.

shots.action: Move past smaller gem-bearing peaks, trees, vines, shrubs and waterfalls, ending at emerald-green foothills touched by Ocean of Milk waves; narration L005–L008. No lake, elephant, crocodile or invented incident.
shots.camera: Slow descending travel shot with gentle cut to shoreline; do not treat the ocean as the freshwater lake.
shots.sound: Distinct waterfall wash, then waves; leave a brief wordless tail for the transition to later S02.

scenes.title: Ṛtumat Garden and the Lotus Lake
scenes.setting: One valley below Trikūṭa, moving from living forest and clear gem-edged waters to Varuṇa's year-round flowering Ṛtumat garden and its immense freshwater lotus lake. This is separate from the Ocean of Milk shoreline seen in S01.
scenes.action: A narrated descent finds bird-rich wooded valleys, then passes through Ṛtumat's evergreen flowers and fruits into a wide, water-level reveal of the golden-lotus lake, its bees, swans, cranes, fish, tortoises and flowering banks. The elephants have not reached the lake in the story yet.
nonverbal_beats: Begin the first shot as a continuous descent from the emerald foothills at the end of S01; birds and forest sounds take over gradually.
Keep Ṛtumat in the valley below Trikūṭa. Varuṇa is identified by narration only; he is not put on-screen as an invented visitor.
In the seasonal garden show mango and coconut trees alongside aśoka/campaka blossoms; do not turn the species list into an unrelated montage.

Reveal one coherent lake with a recognizable tree-lined approach bank, broad golden-lotus zone and deeper center; all placement within the lake is original shot staging, not a claim about the source's compass directions.
Keep waterfowl above and fish/tortoises below the waterline; do not show Gajendra, elephant herd, crocodile or attack in S02.

shots.action: Travel down into the green valley: trees, birds and small animals; glimmering clear streams and gem-like shore stones. Narrator L001–L003 reveals the approach to Ṛtumat without entering the garden lake yet.
shots.camera: Cinematic 16:9 wide descending glide, matching S01's emerald-foot transition; favor an open valley sightline rather than unrelated landscapes.
shots.sound: Continuous birdsong and distant stream; understated original score. NARRATOR offscreen only.

shots.action: Enter Varuṇa's Ṛtumat garden: year-round fruit and blossoms, mango, coconut, aśoka and campaka. Narrator L004–L006 names Varuṇa and shows the garden before the lake reveal.
shots.camera: Medium-wide garden-path tracking with botanical foreground and coherent trees from wide to close views; avoid adding named figures.
shots.sound: Garden birds, delicate bees and foliage breeze; narration stays intelligible, no character voices.

shots.action: Reveal the broad freshwater lake covered with golden lotuses and other water lilies; track bees above the flowers, swans and cranes across the surface, and fish/tortoises disturbing pollen below. Narrator L007–L011; end on stable approach-bank geography for S03 and S04.
shots.camera: Wide lake opening to water-level medium inserts without changing the bank/center relationship. Fish/tortoise shots are separate intentional inserts when frames are authored later.
shots.sound: Bees, swans/cranes, soft rippling water and a short wordless closing tail; no elephant, crocodile or speaking-face lip-sync.

scenes.title: Gajendra Leads the Herd
scenes.setting: A forest trail on Trikūṭa's lower slopes approaching the established Ṛtumat garden and its freshwater lotus lake. The tree-lined approach bank, broad golden-lotus zone and deeper lake center remain geographically consistent with S02.
scenes.action: Introduce the elephant leader Gajendra in his natural form, accompanied by female elephants and younger elephants. His enormous body forces a path through thorny thickets; powerful animals withdraw while smaller creatures roam safely farther away. By late heat, perspiration and thirst show in the group. Bees gather near the leader, and a breeze carries the scent of lotus pollen; the herd follows him to the bank without yet entering the water.
nonverbal_beats: Reveal Gajendra as a naturally moving, four-legged Indian elephant with stable trunk, ears and tusks; no crown, clothing, human hands, speaking-mouth animation or visual reference approval implied.
The herd includes adult females and small calves. Keep calves naturally proportioned and sheltered among adults without inventing named friends or spoken replies.
Bamboo, thorny cane, creepers and clustered shrubs bend and break as Gajendra presses forward. Show the movement as a source-grounded consequence of his size, not unnecessary violence.
Show fierce animals, including lions or tigers, withdrawing in distant background shots; elsewhere deer, rabbits and monkeys move unafraid. Do not suggest all forest creatures flee in terror.
As the elephants grow hot and thirsty, bees hum near Gajendra's temple area and the lotus-scented breeze moves toward the herd; do not attribute supernatural power to the breeze.
End with the elephants arriving at the same approach bank established in S02. No drinking, bathing, spraying, underwater menace or crocodile appears before S04–S06.

shots.action: Introduce Gajendra leading female elephants and calves through thorny cane and thick creepers in Trikūṭa's forest; branches part as the herd advances. Narration L001–L004; keep body shape and forest geography consistent.
shots.camera: 16:9 wide tracking profile into a low three-quarter view of the elephant leader; hold him quadrupedal with identifiable trunk and tusks; no human-like mouth or portrait lip-sync.
shots.sound: Natural heavy footfalls, dry leaves, snapped twigs and distant bird calls under offscreen NARRATOR; no elephant speech.

shots.action: From a safe distant view, lions, tigers, rhinoceroses and serpents withdraw from the elephant's path while small deer and rabbits continue peacefully elsewhere; cut to the herd's massive footfalls. Narration L005–L008.
shots.camera: Intercut a readable broad forest map, retreating powerful animals and a separate calm forest clearing. Never crop a fleeing animal into the elephant's exact location or imply attacks.
shots.sound: Underbrush rustle, retreating pawsteps and subdued forest ambience; use no invented dialogue or frightening animal confrontation.

shots.action: Heat and thirst affect the moving herd. Bees circle near Gajendra's temples; the leader lifts his trunk to scent lotus pollen on a breeze and the elephants hurry to the established approach bank. Hold at the shore before water entry. Narration L009–L011.
shots.camera: Medium close-up of natural trunk and head, then wide follow shot from behind toward the recognizable lotus lake. Preserve the S02 bank/center/lotus-zone relationship for S04.
shots.sound: Bees near the elephant, warm breeze, approaching lake birds and gentle water ambience. Offscreen NARRATOR; end with a brief environmental tail before S04.

scenes.title: Thirst and Relief at the Water
scenes.setting: The previously established near approach bank of the freshwater lotus lake in Varuṇa's Ṛtumat garden; clear cool water is flecked with lotus and water-lily pollen. This is not the Ocean of Milk shoreline. The same tree line, lotus band and deeper center remain consistently oriented.
scenes.action: Gajendra enters the clear water at the near bank, bathes and lifts it with his trunk to drink until satisfied. With his fatigue eased, he draws up water to share with female elephants and calves, sprinkling and helping them drink and bathe. He remains absorbed in their comfort and does not reflect on possible hardship. No crocodile or hostile movement appears; the scriptural grip occurs only in verse 8.2.27, reserved for S06.
nonverbal_beats: Match S03's final approach-bank camera direction and S02's one coherent freshwater lake; start with Gajendra's natural four legs entering at the near shoreline and retain stable tusks, ears and trunk.
Keep bathing and drinking distinct: Gajendra bathes, then uses his trunk to draw cool, clear, lotus-pollen water to drink; water behavior remains naturalistic, not human-style hand gestures.
Female elephants and calves remain visibly grouped near the shallower bank. Show water shared by the leader without inventing a conversation, laughter, a contest or human faces on animals.
Gajendra can spray water from his trunk onto nearby herd members and aid their drinking/bathing, as the account states. Give the calves safe scale relative to adults.

Close on Gajendra caring for the herd and an ordinary ripple with a brief contemplative narrator line. Do not show a lurking crocodile, shadow, incoming threat, supernatural warning or attack in this verse-25–26 scene.
All on-screen animal sounds and splashes are ambience/effects; none are spoken audio tracks or approved recordings.

shots.action: Continue from S03's established bank as Gajendra steps into the lotus lake; the water is cold and clear with drifting pollen. He bathes naturally, showing fatigue easing; narration L001–L003. No crocodile visible.
shots.camera: 16:9 medium-wide bank-to-water follow with a brief readable water-level angle; foreground bank stays the same as S02/S03 and body anatomy remains quadrupedal.
shots.sound: Continuous lake birds, light sloshing and water against the bank under the offscreen narrator. No animal speech or threat cue.

shots.action: Gajendra raises water with his trunk, drinks until satisfied, and bathes again to wash away the long walk's fatigue; narration L004–L007. Preserve trunk and tusks across shot reverses.
shots.camera: Natural-profile medium detail on trunk drawing water, followed by medium-wide bathing without crossing the pre-established lake geography.
shots.sound: Trunk suction/soft splash textures and calm water ambience. Keep narration clear and leave brief natural pauses.

shots.action: Female elephants and calves join Gajendra at the shallows. He lifts water in his trunk, sprinkles them and helps them drink and bathe, absorbed in caring for the herd; narration L008–L011. End on a calm family grouping, without an ominous underwater cut.
shots.camera: Stable 16:9 wide family group at the same shore, with a short medium view of Gajendra's natural trunk spray. Avoid humanlike gestures and animal mouth lip-sync.
shots.sound: Gentle trunk-water spray, calf splashes, birds, and a soft environmental tail. The narrator is the only spoken owner.

scenes.title: The Calm Beneath the Surface
scenes.setting: The same tree-lined shallow bank, surface lotus patch and wider freshwater lake established in S02–S04. The title names a reflective pause only: no underwater or predator-view shot is authored, and no new scriptural event is implied.
scenes.action: A short, source-disclosed visual transition after Gajendra has helped the herd bathe and drink. His attention remains on the elephants (SB 8.2.26). The final droplets slip from his trunk while a calf stands beside its mother, and ordinary ripples settle among the lotus leaves. The calf's placement and the settling water are original screenplay staging, not separate incidents described in the source. End without a crocodile, a mysterious shadow, a threat cue, or an invented warning; the first grip is left to verse 8.2.27 and S06.
nonverbal_beats: S05 is deliberately shortened from the original 60-second planning allowance to a 30-second bridge. Verse 26 is brief and S04 already dramatized its substantive water-sharing action. Do not pad this passage with unrelated wildlife or repeated splash montages.
Continue directly from S04's last grouping: Gajendra with female elephants and calves in the established shallows, now with fewer large water splashes; quadruped anatomy stays natural.
A calf remains close to its mother while the last normal droplets fall from Gajendra's trunk. This precise visual blocking is original dramatization rather than a newly found scriptural beat.

Hold on ordinary surface ripples and golden lotus leaves from the same bank. Use no underwater camera, lurking eye, crocodile silhouette, camera stalk, ominous score, supernatural forewarning, or other suggestion that 8.2.25–26 depicts an approaching predator.
Use natural lake sound and a measured narrator pause. No spoken elephant voice, text on screen, approved artwork or recordings.

shots.action: Resume S04's concluding herd composition. Gajendra looks toward the female elephants and calves as the vigorous splashing subsides; narration L001 reflects the source's focus on family. The pause is a cinematic continuation of 8.2.26, not a new plot event.
shots.camera: Fixed medium-wide 16:9 at the previously established near bank with the golden-lotus zone behind; avoid reversing the herd's direction or changing the shoreline.
shots.sound: Only existing natural shore ambience, water drops and offscreen NARRATOR. No animal dialogue or ominous cue.

shots.action: A calf stands close to its mother while the last small water droplets fall from Gajendra's trunk; narration L002. This small relational insert is explicitly original nonverbal staging drawn from the animals already present in 8.2.26.
shots.camera: Simple medium detail of natural elephant mother/calf spacing with Gajendra's trunk at frame edge; do not manufacture a new named calf or human expressions.
shots.sound: Quiet individual drops and natural herd movements; NARRATOR only. No lip-sync.

shots.action: On the same lake surface, small ripples fade around already established lotus leaves. Narration L003–L004 ends with a brief quiet pause. Stop before 8.2.27; no crocodile or attack image.
shots.camera: Shoreline-facing medium-wide cutaway that retains the prior bank and lotus geometry; no underwater shot, POV pursuit, shadows or threat foreshadowing.
shots.sound: Soft water and birds, then a brief quiet environmental tail without dramatic sting.

scenes.title: The Crocodile's Sudden Grip
scenes.setting: Same freshwater lotus lake in Varuṇa's Ṛtumat garden, at the previously established shallow approach bank. The bank remains to the left in the editorial master view and deeper water toward the right. The crocodile becomes visible only when it seizes Gajendra's leg here; exact leg and camera orientation are original shot decisions, not verse facts.
scenes.action: Immediately after the peaceful surface view at the end of S05, a strong crocodile abruptly catches Gajendra's leg while he is in the water. Gajendra braces and exerts his strength to escape, but the grip remains. The female elephants cry out and other elephants approach to assist, beginning the response described in SB 8.2.28. Stop with Gajendra still caught; the herd's unsuccessful coordinated rescue, changes in water-versus-land advantage, and long struggle are left to S01E02.
nonverbal_beats: No crocodile silhouette, shadow, lurking eye, stealth approach or threatening sound appears in S01–S05. The crocodile's first visible action is the sudden leg-grip in S06, matching SB 8.2.27.

For repeatable screen geography, the crocodile takes Gajendra's left foreleg in the near shallows, with the lake's deeper center beyond. The verse says only 'foot/leg'; the selected side is an original editorial design choice and must be consistent in every later angle.

Keep Gajendra naturally quadrupedal with a stable elephant head, tusks and trunk; show the crocodile as a believable animal with a single jaw, tail and consistent scale. Neither animal speaks, uses human lips or has a dramatic human facial expression.
Make the grip and Gajendra's attempt to pull free readable in medium-wide body blocking. Do not show blood, broken skin, injury closeups, dismemberment, savage bite detail, or impact spectacle.

Female elephants cry out, as SB 8.2.28 recounts. Other adults begin to approach him and calves remain among the herd. Do not yet stage the failed pull-from-behind outcome or thousand-year montage that S01E02 needs to portray in detail.

Water splashes, controlled camera timing and the choice of a brief suspenseful pause are original cinematography/SFX; not newly claimed events or direct words from scripture. Sound may convey urgency without horror.

shots.action: Cut from S05's calm lotus surface to a clean, readable waterline wide shot: a powerful crocodile suddenly grips Gajendra's left foreleg. This is the animal's first appearance; narration L001–L002. Keep the contact non-graphic, with no earlier approach, stalking or unverified scene.
shots.camera: 16:9 stable medium-wide side view from the established near bank, with Gajendra's full body, one restrained foreleg and crocodile body geography legible; no predatory point-of-view or injury close-up.
shots.sound: Sudden water displacement, a brief restrained natural impact, offscreen NARRATOR. No scream dubbed as human dialogue and no horror sting.

shots.action: Gajendra plants his other feet and strains to pull his seized leg back toward the bank; the crocodile keeps the hold. Narration L003–L006. Natural splashing is explicitly cinematographic elaboration, not a separate account of extended combat.
shots.camera: Hold a wide full-body axis and one natural leg/trunk detail, retaining the lake's deep-water direction and the originally designated left foreleg. Avoid impossible joint bending or changing which leg is caught.
shots.sound: Heavy water movement, elephant distress call as nonverbal SFX, and clear narration; no blood sounds, human speech or prolonged fight montage.

shots.action: Female elephants see Gajendra and call out. Other elephants begin moving to help him, but the final frame holds on his still-trapped leg, with no successful release. Narration L007–L009; defer the verse-28 failed pulling effort and the verse-29 thousand-year conflict to S01E02.
shots.camera: Return to the master bank-facing 16:9 wide shot, herd near shallow water, calves behind the adults, Gajendra and crocodile at the same location; end as a respectful non-graphic cliffhanger.
shots.sound: Natural elephant calls and rushing water beneath NARRATOR. Cut after a short suspended beat; no invented spoken animal dialogue.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Open the ancient setting through a calm, grounded narrator.

text.te: శుక మహర్షి ఒక రాజుకు ఓ అద్భుతమైన పర్వతం గురించి చెప్పారు. దాని పేరు త్రికూటం.
text.hi: शुकदेव मुनि ने एक राजा को एक अद्भुत पर्वत के बारे में बताया। उसका नाम था त्रिकूट।
text.en: Śukadeva told a king about a magnificent mountain called Trikūṭa.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Establish the mythic ocean and mountain scale.

text.te: దాని చుట్టూ క్షీరసాగరం ఉంది. ఆ సముద్రం మధ్య త్రికూటం ఎంతో ఎత్తుగా నిలిచింది.
text.hi: उसके चारों ओर क्षीरसागर था। उस समुद्र के बीच त्रिकूट बहुत ऊँचा खड़ा था।
text.en: The Ocean of Milk surrounded it, and Trikūṭa rose high above the waves.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Name each distinct material without rushing
dialogue.intent: Differentiate the three defining peaks.

text.te: త్రికూటానికి మూడు ప్రధాన శిఖరాలు ఉన్నాయి. ఒకటి బంగారంతో, ఒకటి వెండితో, మరొకటి ఇనుముతో.
text.hi: त्रिकूट की तीन मुख्य चोटियाँ थीं—एक सोने की, एक चाँदी की और एक लोहे की।
text.en: Trikūṭa had three great peaks: one of gold, one of silver and one of iron.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Hold on the complete three-peak silhouette.

text.te: ఆ మూడు శిఖరాలు ఆకాశానికీ, చుట్టూ ఉన్న దిక్కులకీ అందం తెచ్చాయి.
text.hi: वे तीनों चोटियाँ आकाश और चारों दिशाओं की शोभा बढ़ाती थीं।
text.en: Those three peaks made the sky and every direction more beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Move from the main peaks to the smaller jewel-rich slopes.

text.te: ఇతర శిఖరాల్లో రత్నాలు, ఎన్నో రకాల ఖనిజాలు మెరిసేవి.
text.hi: दूसरी चोटियों पर तरह-तरह के रत्न और खनिज चमकते थे।
text.en: Other peaks held precious stones and many kinds of minerals.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Reveal the vegetation without adding new characters or events.

text.te: చెట్లు, తీగలు, పొదలు ఆ కొండలంతా విస్తరించాయి.
text.hi: पेड़, बेलें और झाड़ियाँ उन ढलानों पर फैली थीं।
text.en: Trees, climbing vines and shrubs spread across the slopes.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Flowing, with a slight pause for the water sound
dialogue.intent: Let the waterfall sound bridge into the final shoreline view.

text.te: జలపాతాలు కిందికి పారుతూ, ఆ పర్వతమంతా నీటి శబ్దంతో మారుమోగేలా చేశాయి.
text.hi: झरने नीचे बहते थे, और उनके पानी की आवाज़ पूरे पहाड़ पर गूँजती थी।
text.en: Waterfalls poured down, and the sound of rushing water echoed across the mountain.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Complete the geographical reveal at the emerald-green foothills.

text.te: పర్వతం అడుగున క్షీరసాగరపు అలలు తాకుతున్నాయి. అక్కడి నేల పచ్చని మరకత రాళ్లతో మెరిసింది.
text.hi: पहाड़ की तलहटी को क्षीरसागर की लहरें छूती थीं। वहाँ की धरती हरे पन्नों से चमकती थी।
text.en: At the mountain’s foot, the ocean waves washed the shore, where green emeralds gleamed.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Quiet wonder; invite us down into the valley
dialogue.intent: Locate the living valleys below Trikūṭa

text.te: త్రికూట పర్వతం దిగువనున్న పచ్చని లోయల్లో పక్షుల కిలకిలలు వినిపించేవి.
text.hi: त्रिकूट की हरी ढलानों के नीचे घाटियों में पक्षियों की चहचहाहट गूँजती थी।
text.en: Below Trikūṭa's green slopes, birds sang throughout the valleys.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show clear water and jewel-like shorelines

text.te: అక్కడ నదులు, సరస్సుల్లో నీళ్లు ఎంతో స్వచ్ఛంగా ఉండేవి. వాటి ఒడ్డున ఇసుక రేణువుల్లాంటి చిన్న రత్నాలు మెరిసేవి.
text.hi: वहाँ नदियों और झीलों का पानी एकदम साफ़ था। उनके किनारों पर रेत के कणों जैसे छोटे-छोटे रत्न चमकते थे।
text.en: Clear rivers and lakes shimmered there. Their shores glittered with tiny gems, as small as grains of sand.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Introduce the name gently, with a pause
dialogue.intent: Name the valley garden without adding new events

text.te: ఆ లోయల్లో ఒక అందమైన తోట ఉండేది. దాని పేరు ఋతుమత్.
text.hi: उन्हीं घाटियों में एक सुंदर बगीचा था। उसका नाम था ऋतुमत।
text.en: In one valley was a beautiful garden called Ṛtumat.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Identify the garden's owner

text.te: ఆ తోట వరుణదేవుడిది.
text.hi: यह बगीचा वरुण देव का था।
text.en: The garden belonged to Varuṇa.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Establish year-round flowers and fruit

text.te: అక్కడ ఏ కాలమైనా పూలు పూసేవి, పండ్లు కాసేవి.
text.hi: वहाँ हर मौसम में फूल खिलते और फल लगते थे।
text.en: Flowers bloomed and fruit grew there in every season.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Give the tree names time to land
dialogue.intent: Show a few representative tree species listed in scripture

text.te: మామిడి, కొబ్బరి చెట్ల మధ్య అశోక, సంపెంగ పూల చెట్లు కూడా ఉండేవి.
text.hi: आम और नारियल के पेड़ों के बीच अशोक और चंपा के फूल भी खिले रहते थे।
text.en: Mango and coconut trees stood near flowering aśoka and campaka trees.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Reveal the central lake and golden lotuses

text.te: ఆ తోటలో ఒక పెద్ద సరస్సు ఉండేది. అందులో బంగారు తామరపూలు మెరిసేవి.
text.hi: उसी बगीचे में एक विशाल झील थी, जिसमें सुनहरे कमल चमकते थे।
text.en: In that garden stretched a broad lake, shining with golden lotuses.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Distinguish other water lilies from golden lotus

text.te: ఆ తామరల మధ్య ఎన్నో రకాల కలువపూలు వికసించేవి.
text.hi: उन कमलों के बीच कई तरह के जल-फूल खिले थे।
text.en: Other kinds of water lilies bloomed between the lotus leaves.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: A little livelier; preserve a natural pause
dialogue.intent: Introduce bees and water birds without characters speaking

text.te: పూల చుట్టూ తేనెటీగలు గుయ్యుమనేవి. నీళ్లపై హంసలు, కొంగలు తిరుగుతూ కూసేవి.
text.hi: फूलों के पास भँवरे गुनगुनाते थे। झील में हंस तैर रहे थे और पास ही सारस पुकार रहे थे।
text.en: Bees hummed near the blossoms; swans and cranes called over the water.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Describe fish, turtles and moving lotus pollen

text.te: చేపలు, తాబేళ్లు కదలడంతో సరస్సు నీళ్లు అలలయ్యాయి. అందులో కలిసిన తామర పుప్పొడి కూడా కదిలింది.
text.hi: मछलियों और कछुओं की हलचल से झील का पानी लहराने लगा। उसमें मिला कमल का पराग भी घूमने लगा।
text.en: Fish and tortoises stirred the lake water, swirling lotus pollen through the ripples.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Hold on the full ring of blooming lakeshore trees

text.te: సరస్సు చుట్టూ పూలు, పండ్లు ఇచ్చే చెట్లు నిండుగా పెరిగేవి.
text.hi: झील के चारों ओर फूलों और फलों से भरे पेड़ थे।
text.en: Flowering and fruit-bearing trees surrounded the lake on every side.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Name the mighty elephant leader without staging a coronation

text.te: త్రికూటం అడవుల్లో గజేంద్రుడు అనే బలమైన ఏనుగు తన గుంపుకు ముందుగా నడిచేవాడు.
text.hi: त्रिकूट के जंगलों में गजेन्द्र नाम का एक विशाल हाथी अपने झुंड के आगे चलता था।
text.en: In Trikūṭa's forest, a mighty elephant named Gajendra led his herd.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Establish females and calves following their leader

text.te: ఆడ ఏనుగులు అతని పక్కనే నడిచేవి. చిన్న ఏనుగులు వాటి వెనక వచ్చేవి.
text.hi: हथिनियाँ उसके साथ चलती थीं और छोटे हाथी उनके पीछे-पीछे आते थे।
text.en: Female elephants walked beside him, and the young ones followed behind.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show the thorny obstacles in the path

text.te: దారంతా ముళ్ల తీగలు, దట్టమైన పొదలతో నిండిపోయింది.
text.hi: रास्ता काँटेदार बेलों और घनी झाड़ियों से भरा हुआ था।
text.en: Thorny vines and thick bushes crowded the path ahead.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show the elephant breaking vegetation as the source describes

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు ముందుకు సాగుతుంటే కొమ్మలు, పొదలు విరిగిపోయాయి.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र आगे बढ़ा तो टहनियाँ और झाड़ियाँ टूटती चली गईं।
text.en: As Gajendra pushed ahead, branches and shrubs snapped in his way.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show lions and tigers retreating at his scent

text.te: అతని వాసన తగలగానే సింహాలు, పులులు కూడా భయపడి దూరంగా పారిపోయాయి.
text.hi: उसकी गंध पाकर शेर और बाघ भी डरकर दूर भाग गए।
text.en: Even lions and tigers fled when they caught his scent.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Other powerful animals leave the elephant's way

text.te: ఖడ్గమృగాలు, పెద్ద పాములు కూడా అతని దారి నుంచి తప్పుకున్నాయి.
text.hi: गैंडे और बड़े साँप भी उसके रास्ते से हट गए।
text.en: Rhinoceroses and great snakes moved away from him too.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Keep smaller animals safe and unafraid elsewhere in the forest

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు చిన్న జంతువులపై దయ చూపేవాడు. అందుకే అడవిలో మరోవైపు జింకలు, కుందేళ్లు, కోతులు భయం లేకుండా తిరిగేవి.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र छोटे जानवरों पर दया करता था। इसलिए जंगल के दूसरे हिस्सों में हिरन, खरगोश और बंदर बिना डरे घूमते थे।
text.en: Because Gajendra treated smaller animals kindly, deer, rabbits and monkeys roamed without fear elsewhere in the forest.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Communicate the elephant's astonishing weight and strength

text.te: అతని బరువైన అడుగులకు కొండంతా కంపించినట్టుగా అనిపించింది.
text.hi: उसके भारी कदमों से मानो पूरा पहाड़ काँप उठा।
text.en: His heavy steps seemed to make the mountain tremble.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Warmth and fatigue rather than distress
dialogue.intent: Show heat, perspiration, bees and thirst without sensationalism

text.te: ఎండకి గజేంద్రుడికి చెమట పట్టింది. గుంపంతా దాహంతో ఉంది. అతని చుట్టూ తేనెటీగలు గుయ్యిమన్నాయి.
text.hi: गर्मी में गजेन्द्र को पसीना आ रहा था। पूरे झुंड को प्यास लगी थी और उसके पास भँवरे गुनगुना रहे थे।
text.en: The heat made Gajendra sweat. The herd was thirsty, and bees hummed around him.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Invite the audience to notice the change in the wind
dialogue.intent: Reveal lotus pollen scent from the established freshwater lake

text.te: అప్పుడే సరస్సు నుంచి తామరపూల పుప్పొడి సువాసన గాలిలో తేలి వచ్చింది.
text.hi: तभी झील की ओर से हवा में कमल के पराग की सुगंध आने लगी।
text.en: Then a breeze carried the scent of lotus pollen from the lake.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Forward momentum, then gentle end pause
dialogue.intent: Finish at the familiar lake bank without beginning bathing

text.te: ఆ వాసన వైపు గజేంద్రుడు త్వరగా నడిచాడు. అతని గుంపంతా సరస్సు ఒడ్డుకు చేరుకుంది.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र उस सुगंध की ओर तेज़ी से बढ़ा और उसका पूरा झुंड झील के किनारे पहुँच गया।
text.en: Gajendra hurried toward that scent, and his herd reached the lake's edge.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Gajendra enters the freshwater lake from the established bank

text.te: సరస్సు ఒడ్డుకు చేరుకున్న గజేంద్రుడు నీళ్లలోకి దిగాడు.
text.hi: झील के किनारे से गजेन्द्र पानी में उतर गया।
text.en: At the lake's edge, Gajendra stepped into the water.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: The cold clear lotus lake offers physical relief

text.te: చల్లగా, స్వచ్ఛంగా ఉన్న నీళ్లు అతని అలసిన ఒంటికి హాయినిచ్చాయి.
text.hi: ठंडे, साफ़ पानी ने उसके थके शरीर को राहत दी।
text.en: The cool, clear water soothed his tired body.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show pollen of lotus and water lilies mixing with lake water

text.te: తామర, కలువ పూల పుప్పొడి సరస్సు నీళ్లలో కలిసింది.
text.hi: कमल और जलकुमुदिनी के फूलों का पराग झील के पानी में मिला हुआ था।
text.en: Lotus and water-lily pollen mingled with the lake water.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Describe Gajendra using his trunk to drink

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు తొండంతో నీళ్లు తీసుకుని తాగాడు.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र ने सूँड से पानी उठाकर पिया।
text.en: Gajendra lifted water with his trunk and drank.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: He drinks until satisfied

text.te: దాహం తీరేవరకు నీళ్లు తాగాడు.
text.hi: उसने तब तक पानी पिया, जब तक उसकी प्यास बुझ नहीं गई।
text.en: He drank until his thirst was gone.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Gajendra bathes with the lake water

text.te: తర్వాత తొండంతో తన ఒంటిమీద నీళ్లు చల్లుకున్నాడు.
text.hi: फिर उसने अपनी सूँड से शरीर पर पानी डाला।
text.en: Then he poured water over himself with his trunk.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: His long journey's fatigue fades

text.te: ఎంతోసేపు నడిచిన అలసట మెల్లగా తగ్గిపోయింది.
text.hi: लंबी यात्रा की थकान धीरे-धीरे मिट गई।
text.en: The tiredness from the long walk began to fade.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: He includes the herd in the relief, not inventing speech

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు తన గుంపులోని ఏనుగులకూ నీళ్లు అందించాడు.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र ने अपने झुंड के बाकी हाथियों को भी पानी दिया।
text.en: Gajendra shared the water with the rest of his herd.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Sprinkle nearby females and calves with the trunk

text.te: తొండంతో నీళ్లు చల్లి ఆడ ఏనుగుల్నీ పిల్ల ఏనుగుల్నీ తడిపాడు.
text.hi: उसने सूँड से हथिनियों और छोटे हाथियों पर पानी छिड़का।
text.en: With his trunk, he sprinkled the female elephants and calves.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Help the herd drink and bathe

text.te: వాళ్లు నీళ్లు తాగి స్నానం చేసేలా కూడా సాయపడ్డాడు.
text.hi: उसने उन्हें पानी पीने और नहाने में भी मदद की।
text.en: He helped them drink and bathe, too.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Slightly reflective, not a scary threat reveal
dialogue.intent: Scriptural caution: attachment leads him not to consider hardship

text.te: ఆడ ఏనుగుల్నీ పిల్ల ఏనుగుల్నీ చూసుకుంటూ, తనకు ఎంత శ్రమ అవుతోందో గజేంద్రుడు పట్టించుకోలేదు.
text.hi: उनकी देखभाल में वह इतना मग्न था कि अपनी मेहनत की भी परवाह नहीं कर रहा था।
text.en: So absorbed in caring for them, he gave little thought to his own effort.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Gentle reflective cadence, with no ominous implication
dialogue.intent: Summarize Gajendra's attention to the family already described in the prior scene

text.te: గజేంద్రుడి దృష్టంతా తన గుంపులోని ఏనుగులపైనే ఉంది.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र का सारा ध्यान अपने झुंड के हाथियों पर ही था।
text.en: Gajendra's attention was still on the elephants around him.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Warm observational tone; allow drops to be heard
dialogue.intent: Let the existing family tableau settle rather than introduce new action

text.te: గజేంద్రుడి తొండం నుంచి చివరి నీటి చుక్కలు జారుతుండగా, ఒక పిల్ల ఏనుగు తన తల్లి పక్కనే నిలిచింది.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र की सूँड से आख़िरी बूँदें टपक रही थीं। एक छोटा हाथी अपनी माँ के पास खड़ा था।
text.en: The last drops fell from Gajendra's trunk as a calf stayed close to its mother.

source_attribution.note: Original visual continuity insert: a calf beside its mother and the last droplets from Gajendra's trunk are staged, not a separately narrated verse incident.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Return attention from the herd to the known lotus lake surface

text.te: తామరాకుల మధ్య అలలు మెల్లగా వ్యాపించి ఆగిపోయాయి.
text.hi: कमल के पत्तों के बीच पानी की लहरें धीरे-धीरे थम गईं।
text.en: Small ripples spread between the lotus leaves and slowly faded.

source_attribution.note: Original atmospheric insert of normal water movement in the already established lotus lake; not a plot incident or a sign of a crocodile.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Natural closing observation, no sinister emphasis
dialogue.intent: End the transitional scene without a manufactured warning

text.te: ఆ క్షణంలో సరస్సు మళ్లీ ప్రశాంతంగా కనిపించింది.
text.hi: उस पल झील फिर शांत दिखाई दे रही थी।
text.en: For a moment, the lake looked peaceful again.

source_attribution.note: Original brief scenic hold for editorial transition only; the source moves directly to the foot-grip in 8.2.27 and makes no claim of preceding calm or stalking.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Sudden but clear, no horror delivery
dialogue.intent: Introduce the crocodile's first attack from the verse

text.te: అప్పుడే నీళ్లలో ఉన్న బలమైన మొసలి ఒక్కసారిగా గజేంద్రుడి కాలును గట్టిగా పట్టుకుంది.
text.hi: उसी पल पानी में एक ताकतवर मगरमच्छ ने अचानक गजेन्द्र का पैर कसकर पकड़ लिया।
text.en: All at once, a powerful crocodile seized Gajendra's leg in the water.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Describe the mighty elephant's unexpected danger

text.te: ఎంతో బలమైన గజేంద్రుడు కూడా ఊహించని ప్రమాదంలో చిక్కుకున్నాడు.
text.hi: इतना शक्तिशाली गजेन्द्र भी अचानक बड़ी मुसीबत में फँस गया।
text.en: Even the mighty Gajendra was caught in sudden danger.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show Gajendra starting to free the trapped leg

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు వెంటనే తన కాలును విడిపించుకోవడానికి ప్రయత్నించాడు.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र ने तुरंत अपना पैर छुड़ाने की कोशिश की।
text.en: Gajendra tried at once to pull his leg free.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show him using his exceptional strength

text.te: తన బలమంతా పెట్టి ఆ కాలును వెనక్కి లాగాడు.
text.hi: उसने पूरी ताकत लगाकर पैर पीछे खींचा।
text.en: He pulled back with all his strength.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Make the crocodile's resistance explicit

text.te: కానీ మొసలి తన పట్టును వదల్లేదు.
text.hi: लेकिन मगरमच्छ की पकड़ ढीली नहीं हुई।
text.en: But the crocodile would not let go.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Short visual narration over water effects
dialogue.intent: Describe non-graphic water movement as original physical staging

text.te: గజేంద్రుడు తన కాలును విడిపించుకోవడానికి పెనుగులాడుతుంటే, చుట్టూ సరస్సు నీళ్లు పైకి చిమ్మాయి.
text.hi: उनकी हलचल से झील का पानी उछलने लगा।
text.en: Water splashed around them as Gajendra struggled.

source_attribution.note: Original non-graphic water-splash staging to make the verse-27 effort readable; scripture does not specify the exact splashes or camera viewpoint.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Show the female elephants' cries without human dialogue

text.te: గజేంద్రుడి కష్టం చూసి ఆడ ఏనుగులు గట్టిగా అరవసాగాయి.
text.hi: गजेन्द्र को संकट में देखकर हथिनियाँ ज़ोर से पुकारने लगीं।
text.en: The female elephants saw his trouble and cried out.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.intent: Begin the other elephants' help but reserve failed pulling for next episode

text.te: మిగతా ఏనుగులు కూడా అతనికి సాయం చేయడానికి దగ్గరకు వచ్చాయి.
text.hi: बाकी हाथी भी उसकी मदद के लिए पास आने लगे।
text.en: Other elephants moved toward their leader to help.

dialogue.speaker: NARRATOR
dialogue.delivery: Quiet unresolved ending, short beat afterward
dialogue.intent: Leave Gajendra still trapped as the episode cliffhanger

text.te: అయినా గజేంద్రుడి కాలు మొసలి పట్టులోనే ఉంది.
text.hi: फिर भी गजेन्द्र का पैर मगरमच्छ की पकड़ में फँसा रहा।
text.en: Yet Gajendra's leg remained caught in the crocodile's grip.
